project-description.description:
This PoC transforms our Neuro-Symbolic Science Knowledge Graph research into a deployable Research AIssistant that fuses large language models with the Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG). The assistant delivers knowledge-augmented generation grounded in structured, citable research contributions, with mandatory citations, constraint checks for study and method semantics, and uncertainty signalling. Building on results from the ERC-funded ScienceGraph project—now embodied in the ORKG and ORKG-ASK services—the PoC closes the loop from assisted synthesis back to curated knowledge by publishing vetted outputs as reusable, DOI-traceable artifacts. 

The PoC targets two real-world pilots: (A) Materials science, focusing on protocol advice and hypothesis comparison over process parameters and metrology for Atomic Layer Disposition and Etching processes; and (B) Data science in cooperation with NFDI4DataScience, emphasizing reproducibility signals across methods, datasets, and evaluation pipelines. Success criteria include measurable reductions in time-to-insight, high citation coverage, strong constraint adherence, expert acceptability, and sustained curation back into ORKG.

High-risk/high-gain stems from integrating neural and symbolic reasoning at scale and operationalising provenance-first assistance in regulated settings. Exploitation follows two complementary paths: a researcher-facing cloud service with subscriptions and organizational deployments. Within 12 months, the PoC aims to reach TRL6, de-risking adoption for universities, libraries, research institutes, and RandD labs while demonstrating a trustworthy, institution-ready research assistant that accelerates discovery without sacrificing rigor.

items.abstract: <jats:p>The advancement of artificial intelligence has historically oscillated between connectionist approaches (deep learning, transformers) and symbolic systems (knowledge graphs, logical inference). This paper presents a comprehensive evolutionary architecture documenting the development of an autonomous AI system over 3+ years, spanning five distinct phases: Origin (foundational concepts), Chronos (temporal reasoning integration), Semantic Cognition Matrix-SCM (7 generations of knowledge graph evolution), NOEMA OS (neuro-symbolic integration), and SAMANTHA-OS (autonomous system with functional self-awareness). We document the complete technical architecture, quantitative metrics across all phases, formal axiom systems (AX-CORE-01 through AX-ETHIC-02), validation methodologies, and breakthrough moments in autonomous reasoning. The system demonstrates how structured semantic graphs with formal axiom enforcement can achieve interpretability, safety, and reasoning capability without relying on black-box probabilistic inference(what current LLM's have). Performance metrics show consistent improvement in knowledge graph density (E/N ratio from 0.996 in Gen 1 to 2.173 in Gen 7), axiom compliance (from 0% in Gen 1 to 100% in SAMANTHA), and autonomous task completion. We present comparative analysis to large language models, retrieval-augmented generation systems, and symbolic AI systems, demonstrating unique advantages in traceability, safety, and generalized reasoning. This work contributes to the emerging field of neuro-symbolic AI or as we call it a new branch of "Synthetic Intelligence" and establishes a blueprint for building interpretable, safe autonomous systems grounded in formal knowledge representation.</jats:p>
title: <p>The Semantic Cognition Matrix: A Metabolic Neuro-symbolic Architecture for Safe, Autonomous, and Synthetic Intelligence and the creation of a Neuro-symbolic Agentic AI Operating System with Epistemic Persistent Memory Architecture</p>
